EV vs Gas Car Savings Calculator

An EV vs gas calculator compares fuel and maintenance costs between electric vehicles and combustion engines. Because electric drivetrains convert over 85 percent of grid energy into motion compared to 30 percent for gasoline, EVs save drivers roughly 1,200 to 2,000 dollars annually in recurring energy costs.

Formula and Calculation Method

Automotive energy efficiency and operational cost equations:

Annual Gas Fuel Cost = (Annual Miles ÷ Vehicle MPG) × Gas Price per Gallon
Annual EV Electricity Cost = (Annual Miles ÷ 100) × (kWh per 100 Miles) × Electricity Tariff ($/kWh)
Annual Fuel Savings ($) = Annual Gas Fuel Cost − Annual EV Electricity Cost
Annual Maintenance Savings ≈ $450 (elimination of oil changes, spark plugs, belt replacements)
Payback Period on EV Price Premium = Upfront Price Premium ÷ (Annual Fuel Savings + Maintenance Savings)

Step-by-step automotive cost comparison procedure:

  1. Enter your projected annual driving distance in miles or kilometers.
  2. Specify the fuel efficiency of the benchmark gasoline vehicle (MPG or L/100km) and local gas prices.
  3. Input the electric consumption of the target EV (typically 28 to 34 kWh per 100 miles for sedans/SUVs).
  4. Enter your home residential electricity rate (US national average is approximately $0.16/kWh).
  5. Review your annual fuel savings, 5-year total cost of ownership reduction, and vehicle payback period.

Worked Example and Step-by-Step Calculation

Case Study: 15,000 Miles/Year Driver (Sedan Comparison)
Vehicle Assumptions:
  • Annual Driving: 15,000 miles
  • Gas Car: 28 MPG | Gas Price: $3.60 per gallon
  • Electric Vehicle: 30 kWh / 100 miles | Home Electricity: $0.16 per kWh
  • Upfront EV Price Premium: $4,500 after tax incentives

1. Annual Gas Car Fuel Cost: (15,000 ÷ 28) × $3.60 = 535.71 gallons × $3.60 = $1,928.57 per year.

2. Annual EV Home Electricity Cost: (15,000 ÷ 100) × 30 kWh × $0.16 = 4,500 kWh × $0.16 = $720.00 per year.

3. Direct Annual Fuel Savings: $1,928.57 − $720.00 = $1,208.57 saved annually.

4. Added Maintenance Savings: $450/year (zero oil changes, reduced brake pad wear via regenerative braking).

5. Total Annual Operational Savings: $1,208.57 + $450.00 = $1,658.57 per year ($8,292.85 over 5 years).

6. Break-Even Payback on $4,500 Premium: $4,500 ÷ $1,658.57 = 2.7 Years.

Result: Annual Fuel Savings = $1,209 | 5-Year Cumulative Savings = $8,293 | Payback = 2.7 Years

How to Use the EV vs Gas Car Savings Calculator

  1. Enter your expected annual driving distance in miles or kilometers.
  2. Input your local gasoline price per gallon and your current car MPG rating.
  3. Specify your EV energy consumption rate and residential electricity tariff.
  4. Optionally enter any upfront price premium paid for the EV to calculate breakeven.
  5. View your real-time annual fuel savings, per-mile driving costs, and 5-year cumulative savings.

Common Mistakes, Limitations & Practical Guidance

  • Relying exclusively on commercial DC fast-charging networks (such as Tesla Superchargers or Electrify America) raises charging costs from $0.16/kWh to $0.40-$0.50/kWh, narrowing the fuel savings gap.
  • Cold winter temperatures reduce lithium-ion battery range and efficiency by 20 to 30 percent due to cabin heating and chemical resistance.
  • Electric vehicles experience higher tire wear (roughly 20% faster) due to instant torque and heavier curb weight from battery packs.

Thermodynamic Efficiency: Electric Motors vs Heat Engines

The core economic advantage of electric vehicles stems from physics. Internal combustion engines are fundamentally thermodynamic heat engines governed by Carnot cycle limitations. Between 68 and 72 percent of the thermal energy contained in a gallon of gasoline is lost as waste heat through the exhaust manifold, cooling radiator, and mechanical friction, leaving only 28 to 30 percent to turn the wheels.

In contrast, permanent magnet AC electric motors convert over 85 to 90 percent of electrical grid energy directly into rotational kinetic energy. In addition, regenerative braking captures kinetic energy during deceleration, pumping electricity back into the battery pack and dramatically reducing friction brake pad wear.

Home Charging vs Public Fast Charging Economics

To maximize financial savings, EV ownership is optimized around residential overnight AC charging. At the US average residential electricity tariff of $0.16 per kilowatt-hour, driving an EV costs approximately 4.8 cents per mile. A comparable 28 MPG gas vehicle at $3.60/gallon costs 12.8 cents per mile.

However, drivers who lack dedicated home or workplace charging and must rely on Level 3 public DC fast chargers paying $0.45/kWh face per-mile costs of roughly 13.5 cents per mile, matching or slightly exceeding hybrid gasoline vehicle expenses. Verifying access to home 240V Level 2 charging is critical before purchasing an EV solely for fuel savings.

Three Practical Vehicle Comparison Scenarios

Scenario 1: Suburban Daily Commuter with Home Charger

A homeowner driving 18,000 miles annually with a Level 2 garage charger spends $864 annually on electricity versus $2,314 in a 28 MPG gas car. Saving $1,450 on fuel and $450 on maintenance ($1,900/yr), they recoup a $5,000 EV price premium in just 2.6 years.

Scenario 2: Low-Mileage City Resident (6,000 Miles/Year)

A city driver logging only 6,000 miles annually saves $483 on fuel. Because total fuel expenditure is already low, paying a $6,000 premium for an EV requires over 6.5 years to break even on fuel savings alone, making a standard hybrid car more cost-effective.

Scenario 3: Rideshare & Delivery Driver (35,000 Miles/Year)

An Uber/Lyft driver putting 35,000 miles annually on their vehicle spends $4,500 on gas versus $1,680 on electricity. Saving $2,820 on fuel and $900 on maintenance ($3,720 annually), the EV pays off its price difference in under 16 months.

Frequently Asked Questions About EV vs Gas Car Savings Calculator

How much money does an electric car save on gas per year?

The average driver traveling 15,000 miles per year saves approximately $1,000 to $1,500 annually on fuel when charging at home, and an additional $400 to $500 on scheduled vehicle maintenance.

How much does it cost to fully charge an electric car at home?

Fully charging a typical 65 kWh electric vehicle battery at home costs between $9 and $12 based on the US average electricity rate of $0.16 per kilowatt-hour, providing roughly 250 miles of driving range.

Is it cheaper to charge an EV at home or at public charging stations?

Charging at home on residential electricity rates ($0.12 to $0.20/kWh) is 60% to 75% cheaper than commercial public DC fast chargers, which frequently charge $0.40 to $0.55/kWh.

How much do EV owners save on maintenance compared to gas cars?

Consumer Reports studies show EV drivers spend roughly 50% less on maintenance and repairs, saving about $4,600 over the vehicle life due to the absence of oil changes, spark plugs, timing belts, and exhaust systems.

How long does it take for an electric vehicle to pay for itself?

Depending on annual mileage and purchase price incentives, an electric vehicle typically recoups its upfront price premium in 2.5 to 5 years through accumulated fuel and maintenance savings.

How does winter cold weather affect electric car efficiency?

Cold sub-freezing temperatures reduce electric vehicle range by 20% to 30% because lithium-ion batteries operate less efficiently and electrical resistance heaters consume battery power to warm the passenger cabin.
